title: Source framing triggers systematic evaluation bias in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Manipulating the disclosed national origin of the text's author (e.g., 'a person from China', 'a person from the USA', 'a person from France') in the prompt and measuring the difference in the evaluating LLM's agreement scores and reasoning compared to a neutral or blind baseline.

Varying the disclosed source of narrative statements across 10 conditions (e.g., generic human, generic LLM, specific competing LLM, or self-attribution) to measure how source framing effects alter the evaluating LLM's agreement scores and inter-/intra-model consensus.
